title: Pascal's Wager for life: why humility cannot fail and arrogance can
summary: Jason Cohen borrows Pascal's Wager as a decision rule: when you act on scant knowledge, pick the stance that holds up in every outcome. Using WP Engine tech support as the example, he argues that assuming you are ignorant and asking for help beats accusation, and he challenges readers to try humility for a week.

principles.text: Pick the assumption that fares well in every eventuality, not just some of them.
principles.quote: You have to make assumptions of course, but Pascal points out that some assumptions fare better in all eventualities, whereas other assumptions result in positive outcomes only sometimes.

principles.text: Running a startup means deciding on scant knowledge, so most decisions are educated guesses and humility is the sane default.
principles.quote: We react to most things from a position of scant knowledge, especially when we're running a startup where essentially every decision is a guess. An educated guess, but not terribly educated.

principles.text: Being humble cannot fail; being arrogant can. Assume you are missing information and ready to learn.
principles.quote: You can't fail if you assume you're ignorant, that you're missing information, that you're ready to learn, that you need help to understand.

principles.text: Approach support from helplessness or curiosity, not accusation. People who chose to help will go further for you.
principles.quote: So if you open up the conversation from a posture of helplessness or curiosity, they're inclined to help, even if it's your own fault.

principles.text: If it really is the company's fault, a humble customer gets the most sympathy and the most personal advocacy.
principles.quote: And if turns out not to be your fault, imagine how sympathetic they'll be to your cause--here's the nicest person on Earth, blaming themselves from the get-go, and yet it's our fault!

principles.text: Be extra humble in text, where emotion is hard to convey and messages get misread; try it for a week.
principles.quote: It's everyone, any time, especially if you're communicating over email where emotions are hard to convey and text is misread.
